concepts.def: Meeting needs without harming future generations.
The demand humans place on nature.
Designing out waste and reusing materials.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sustainability — a core area of A-Level Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sustainability brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sustainability.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a renewable resource?
options: Wind energy
Crude oil
Coal
Natural gas

mcqs.q: The area of land and water needed to support a population and absorb its waste is its:
options: Ecological footprint
Carrying capacity
Biodiversity index
Residence time

mcqs.q: Sustainable management of a fishery aims to harvest fish at a rate that:
options: Allows the stock to regenerate
Removes the whole stock quickly
Ignores the breeding rate
Maximises waste

mcqs.q: Sustainable development is best described as meeting present needs while:
options: Not compromising future generations
Using all resources at once
Banning all resource use
Ignoring the environment

mcqs.q: Does 'renewable' mean a resource can never run out?
options: No; renewable resources can still be depleted if used faster than they regenerate, such as overfished stocks.
Yes; renewable resources are unlimited and cannot be exhausted.
Sustainability means stopping all human activity.
Renewable only refers to solar power.

mcqs.q: What does the 'tragedy of the commons' describe?
options: A natural disaster affecting common land.
How shared resources can be overused and degraded when individuals act in their own self-interest.
A law that bans the use of public resources.
Sustainability means stopping all human activity.

mcqs.q: Is economic growth always incompatible with sustainability?
options: No; sustainable development seeks growth that meets present needs without harming future generations' resources.
Sustainability means stopping all human activity.
Yes; any economic growth automatically destroys sustainability.
Renewable only refers to solar power.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Carrying capacity”?
options: Meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs, especially in resource use.
The maximum population size of a species that an environment can support indefinitely given its available resources.
A resource such as coal, oil or natural gas that exists in finite amounts and is not replaced on a human timescale once used.
The area of land and water needed to supply a population's resources and absorb its waste, used to gauge environmental demand.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sustainable management”?
options: Using resources such as fisheries or forests at a rate that allows them to regenerate, for example through quotas and replanting.
The area of land and water needed to supply a population's resources and absorb its waste, used to gauge environmental demand.
The maximum population size of a species that an environment can support indefinitely given its available resources.
A resource such as coal, oil or natural gas that exists in finite amounts and is not replaced on a human timescale once used.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sustainability”?
options: The area of land and water needed to supply a population's resources and absorb its waste, used to gauge environmental demand.
Meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs, especially in resource use.
Using resources such as fisheries or forests at a rate that allows them to regenerate, for example through quotas and replanting.
The maximum population size of a species that an environment can support indefinitely given its available resources.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Non-renewable resource”?
options: Meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs, especially in resource use.
The area of land and water needed to supply a population's resources and absorb its waste, used to gauge environmental demand.
A resource such as coal, oil or natural gas that exists in finite amounts and is not replaced on a human timescale once used.
A resource such as solar, wind or sustainably managed timber that can be replenished naturally within a human timescale.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ecological footprint”?
options: A resource such as solar, wind or sustainably managed timber that can be replenished naturally within a human timescale.
Using resources such as fisheries or forests at a rate that allows them to regenerate, for example through quotas and replanting.
The area of land and water needed to supply a population's resources and absorb its waste, used to gauge environmental demand.
A resource such as coal, oil or natural gas that exists in finite amounts and is not replaced on a human timescale once used.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Renewable resource”?
options: A resource such as coal, oil or natural gas that exists in finite amounts and is not replaced on a human timescale once used.
A resource such as solar, wind or sustainably managed timber that can be replenished naturally within a human timescale.
Using resources such as fisheries or forests at a rate that allows them to regenerate, for example through quotas and replanting.
The maximum population size of a species that an environment can support indefinitely given its available resources.
